skill.name: firecrawl-build-onboarding
skill.description: Guides agents through Firecrawl onboarding for application projects, including browser authorization, API key placement, SDK selection, and first integration setup.
skill.summary: Set up Firecrawl credentials, SDKs, and first app integration steps.
skill.author: firecrawl

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting, documentation links, placeholders, or expected Firecrawl onboarding references. Confirmed risks remain around credential handling, direct `.env` updates, and an unpinned `npx @latest` installer command that executes remote package code.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the CLI to a reviewed version and require explicit user confirmation before running installer commands.

remediation.issue: The auth flow returns an API key to the agent and appends it to `.env`.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for confirmation before writing credentials, avoid logging key values, and prefer a secret manager for shared environments.

remediation.issue: Examples encourage local `.env` storage for credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to verify `.env` is ignored by source control and to use deployment platform secret stores for production.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Remote Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The install instructions run `npx -y firecrawl-cli@latest init --all --browser`, which executes the latest published package without pinning a reviewed version.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command is directly present in the install section and uses both `@latest` and `-y`. The purpose is legitimate, but the supply-chain exposure is real.

semantic_findings.title: Agent-Mediated API Key Persistence
semantic_findings.description: The auth flow documents receiving an `apiKey` from the polling endpoint and then appending a Firecrawl API key to `.env`, placing the agent in the path of a secret.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The endpoint response example includes `apiKey`, and the final step writes a key into `.env`. This is intended onboarding, but it is clear credential handling.

content.value_statement: Teams need a clear path from Firecrawl signup to a working application integration. This skill guides credential setup, SDK choice, and smoke testing for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides browser authorization when the user does not already have a Firecrawl API key.
Shows how to place hosted or self-hosted Firecrawl settings in environment configuration.
Directs agents to SDK installation paths for JavaScript, Python, Rust, Java, Elixir, and REST.
Helps choose between a fresh project setup and an existing project integration path.
Recommends a smoke test after adding the first Firecrawl request.
limitations: Requires the user to complete browser authorization for new Firecrawl credentials.
Does not implement endpoint-specific scraping, crawling, or search behavior by itself.
Depends on external Firecrawl documentation and service availability.
Handles API key setup, so users must protect local environment files and secret stores.

use_cases.title: Add Firecrawl to a New App
use_cases.description: A developer can create credentials, install the right SDK, and add a first verified Firecrawl request.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Setup
use_cases.description: A technical lead can give agents a repeatable process for local, preview, and production credential setup.

use_cases.title: Prepare Self-Hosted Configuration
use_cases.description: A platform engineer can add both the API key and custom Firecrawl API URL for internal deployments.

prompt_templates.title: Start Firecrawl Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a project without credentials.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to set up Firecrawl for this project. Ask me before changing environment files.

prompt_templates.title: Use Existing Key
prompt_templates.scenario: Credential exists and needs to be wired into the app.
prompt_templates.prompt: I already have a Firecrawl API key. Add the correct environment variable guidance and choose the SDK for this stack.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Into Existing Codebase
prompt_templates.scenario: Existing project with established configuration patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the repository configuration patterns, then plan the safest Firecrawl SDK integration and smoke test.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Firecrawl onboarding plan for development, preview, and production using secret managers where possible.

output_examples.input: Set up Firecrawl for a new TypeScript service.
output: Identifies that browser authorization is needed before code changes.
Selects the Node or TypeScript SDK path from the documentation.
Plans an environment variable update and one smoke test request.

output_examples.input: Configure self-hosted Firecrawl in an existing app.
output: Finds the project secret configuration pattern.
Adds guidance for both the API key and custom API URL.
Recommends mirroring the setup across deployment environments.

output_examples.input: Choose how to proceed after credentials are available.
output_examples.output: The skill directs the agent to pick the narrowest Firecrawl endpoint, read the language-specific source page, and run a real smoke test.

best_practices: Ask for user confirmation before creating or modifying environment files.
Use a platform secret manager for shared, preview, or production credentials.
Run one smoke test after SDK installation to prove the key and endpoint work.
anti_patterns: Do not commit `.env` files or Firecrawl API keys to source control.
Do not run unpinned installer commands in regulated environments without review.
Do not choose a broad Firecrawl endpoint before defining the product behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill create a Firecrawl account?
faq.answer: No. It guides the browser authorization flow so the user can sign in or create an account.

faq.question: Can it work with an existing API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide placement of an existing key in environment configuration or a secret manager.

faq.question: Which programming languages are covered?
faq.answer: It links to Firecrawl source pages for Node, Python, Rust, Java, Elixir, and REST usage.

faq.question: Does it write application scraping logic?
faq.answer: No. It prepares credentials and SDK setup, then points to endpoint-specific implementation guidance.

faq.question: Is a self-hosted Firecrawl deployment supported?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes setup guidance for a custom Firecrawl API URL with the API key.

faq.question: What security care is needed?
faq.answer: Protect API keys, avoid committing environment files, and confirm any installer or credential file changes.
